title: Chile's cool fringes
subtitle: Coast, north and south
objectives: Explain the influence of the Humboldt Current

steps.title: The Humboldt Current
steps.body: The cold Humboldt Current runs north along Chile's coast, cooling the air and bringing morning fog. Coastal valleys like Casablanca, San Antonio and Leyda are among Chile's coolest, ideal for Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. This east to west contrast matters more than north to south.

steps.title: Costa, Entre Cordilleras, Andes
steps.body: In 2011 Chile added three descriptors to its regions: Costa, for coastal areas; Entre Cordilleras, between the mountain ranges; and Andes, for the foothills. A Costa wine is likely to be fresh and lower in alcohol; an Andes wine to have firm tannin and freshness from altitude.

steps.prompt: In Chile, distance from the coast often matters more than latitude for climate.
steps.explanation: Yes. The cold Humboldt Current cools coastal areas, while inland valleys get warmer before the Andes cool them again.

steps.title: North and south
steps.body: In the north, Limarí and Elqui have limestone soils and coastal fog, making mineral Chardonnay and Syrah. In the south, Itata, Bío-Bío and Malleco are cooler and wetter, with old dry-farmed vines of País and Cinsault, and new plantings of Riesling and Pinot Noir.
steps.highlight: Limarí in the north; Itata in the south

steps.prompt: Which Chilean region is best known for cool, coastal Sauvignon Blanc?
steps.explanation: Casablanca's coastal location brings fog and cool air, perfect for crisp whites.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The Humboldt Current cools Chile's coast
Costa, Entre Cordilleras and Andes describe position
Limarí and Itata extend Chile north and south
